correctness.rationale: Exact local factors \(\beta(p^a)/p^a\) prove all rational inequalities. For composite \(n\ne4\), \(\beta(n)<n-1\) ensures integer \(K\ge2\). If \(n\) is even with at most four distinct prime factors, oddness of \(\beta(n)\) implies even odd-prime exponents, giving \(\beta(n)/n\ge105/384>1/4\); \(K\) is odd and hence equals \(3\), while \(3\nmid n\) raises the ratio bound to \(385/1152>1/3\), contradiction. For odd integers with at most three distinct primes, \(\beta(n)/n>1/2\) except when their support is \(\{3,5,7\}\), \(\{3,5,11\}\), or \(\{3,5,13\}\). There \(K=2\), the exponent of \(3\) is \(1\), and exact ratio bounds and congruences modulo \(4\), \(3\), and \(5\) exclude each support. The independent finite arithmetic check up to one million supports but does not prove the universal statement.

originality.rationale: The primary 2011 survey poses the exact divisibility \(\beta(n)\mid n-1\) and supplies bounded numerical evidence, not an unrestricted prime-support theorem. The equivalent function \(\rho\) in Iannucci (2006) is investigated for \(k\rho(n)=n\), not the shifted divisibility. A two-prime-support exclusion is strictly weaker than excluding odd integers with \(\omega(n)=3\) and even integers with \(\omega(n)=3\) or \(4\). Actual literature, historical claims, alias, and sequence searches found no covering theorem, with a residual possibility of unindexed earlier proofs.
residual_risks: A covering elementary proof may exist in unindexed historical writing; search absence does not certify global novelty.
Classical Lehmer necessary conditions for squarefree numbers do not directly settle nonsquarefree \(\beta\), but stronger unpublished reductions cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: A concrete question posed in 2011 motivates a complete, exponent-uniform low-prime-support obstruction. Excluding odd integers with \(\omega(n)=3\) and even integers with \(\omega(n)=3\) or \(4\) uses a parity-to-quotient obstruction and exact local congruences. These exclude infinite structurally natural families, without asserting counterexample existence above the boundaries.
